title: Harborlane Pilot: Unit Economics & Benchmark Scoping
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 4-week pilot to validate per-token unit economics and latency/throughput targets for Harborlane's product suggestions and short copy generation. Agreed to share traffic traces and pricing spreadsheet; Redwood to propose a dedicated pilot config with quantized model options and benchmark plan.
next_steps: Maya to send pilot pricing spreadsheet and Dedicated sizing calc
Darius to share a 7-day sample traffic trace and prompt corpus
Liam to draft benchmark script and baseline run plan
Schedule 45-min technical deep-dive next week for infra team
action_items: Maya Patel - Email pilot pricing + sizing spreadsheet - 2026-07-30
Darius Chen - Provide 7-day traffic trace + sample prompts (S3 link) - 2026-08-03
Liam O'Connor - Run baseline latency tests on provided sample set and upload results - 2026-08-05
Priya Sen - Confirm success metrics (p50/p95, cost per order uplift) and stakeholder list - 2026-08-02
transcript:
Header: 2026-07-28 16:30 PDT | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Maya, Liam (Redwood); Sofia, Darius, Priya (Harborlane)

Summary (auto): quick intro, then dive into workload characteristics for checkout suggestion microcopy and product recommendation short texts. Focus on cost/capacity tradeoffs and a 4-week pilot to validate unit economics.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for coming, I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. Quick intros?
[00:08] Sofia: Hi, Sofia Ramirez, Head of ML at Harborlane.
[00:11] Darius: Darius Chen, infra lead.
[00:14] Priya: Priya Sen, product, focusing on conversions.
[00:18] Liam: Liam O'Connor, solutions engineer, I'll handle the bench and sizing stuff.

[00:30] Maya: Cool. The agenda — align on success criteria, look at your traffic and prompts, propose a pilot config (dedicated vs hosted), and sketch a benchmark plan. We have about 45 minutes for technical scoping then next steps. Sound right?
[00:45] Sofia: Yep. Our main thing is we want predictable cost per generated suggestion and p95 latency under 300 ms for interactive flows, but batch jobs can be longer. Also budget cap ~ $25k/month for the initial pilot.
[01:05] Priya: To add product context: these are short prompts, usually 30 to 120 tokens in the request, responses 15 to 80 tokens. Peak traffic spikes during promotions — 3x baseline for 10-20 minutes.
[01:25] Darius: On infra, we want to avoid sending PII to third parties but we can use Redwood's Dedicated or Private if needed. For POC we prefer Dedicated in our region.

[01:40] Liam: Good context — that mix (short-ish prompts, occasional spikes) plays well with batching and prefix caching. For per-token economics it's important to know average sequence lengths and KV cache hit rates. Do you have traces?
[01:55] Darius: We can share a 7-day sample trace, sanitized. It has request timestamps, token counts, and prompt types.
[02:03] Maya: Great. With that we can size a Dedicated pool to hit p95 targets and estimate cost. Quick question — are embeddings used in the same flow or separate?
[02:14] Sofia: Search embeddings are separate — those go into nightly indexing. This pilot is just generation: microcopy and suggestions.

[02:25] Liam: Ok, so we model generation-only. Rough back-of-envelope: if you do 200 RPS sustained with avg request+response tokens of 160 total, that's 200 * 160 = 32k tokens/sec, ~2M tokens/min, which is...phew, sorry I did math out loud. But we need realistic peaks; you mentioned 3x spikes to 600 RPS.
[02:50] Priya: Our baseline is more like 50 RPS by region for now, but projected Q4 growth could push to those higher numbers. We want a pilot that demonstrates cost per order uplift while staying under the $25k runway.

[03:08] Maya: For cost modeling we look at unit token cost for model variants (e.g., 7B float, 7B quantized, 13B), plus overhead for idle capacity, batching efficiencies, and caching. Liam, can you walk through how batching changes per-token cost?
[03:24] Liam: Sure. With continuous batching in Redwood's runtime, per-token amortized GPU time drops with larger batch sizes. For short sequences, naive single-request execution is expensive; batching can cut per-token GPU time by 30-60% depending on model and latency SLO. But you trade off tail latency.
[03:44] Sofia: How do prefix/KV caches factor in for repeated product prompts?
[03:50] Liam: If many requests share the same product prefix — like product title + context — Redwood's prefix KV cache can serve repeated KV states so you only compute incremental tokens. Effective hit-rate reduces GPU work for subsequent requests. We'll need your trace to estimate hit-rate.
[04:06] Darius: Our UX often reuses templates, so I expect reasonable prefix reuse. We'll mark those in the trace.

[04:15] Maya: Pilot config options: 1) Hosted: quickest to start, per-token pricing, limited control over instance types; 2) Dedicated small pool: reserved GPU instances in your region with predictable throughput and caching control; 3) Private: for on-prem but longer lead time. For your security needs, Dedicated seems best for pilot.
[04:40] Priya: Dedicated sounds right. Can you give a recommended starter profile?
[04:45] Liam: Based on what you've said, a starter could be 4x A10G or 2x H100 (time-shared) depending on model. If we use a quantized 7B with good batching and caching, 4 A10Gs should hit p95 under 300ms for most requests at baseline, and sustain spikes with queuing + autoscale. We'll run a sizing calc once we get traces.
[05:08] Sofia: H100 is attractive for peak throughput but we care about cost per token. Is quantization supported on your runtime?
[05:16] Liam: Yes — Redwood supports 4-bit/8-bit quantized execution paths. Quantized models often cut VRAM and increase throughput at a small quality delta; we can show quality vs cost tradeoffs in the bench.
[05:30] Priya: On quality: we need no regression on conversion metrics — if suggestions get worse we stop. How do we guard that?
[05:39] Maya: We define acceptance criteria: A/B test improvement or non-inferiority on clickthrough/conversion, and automated quality monitors on prompts/evals during pilot. We'll instrument the experiment.

[05:52] Darius: From infra side, how do we measure token accounting? We need token-level billing and per-route cost breakdown to reconcile with internal cost center.
[06:02] Maya: Redwood Console exports token-level metrics and cost per route. We'll include that in pilot deliverables.

[06:12] Liam: For the benchmark plan: we run three phases — baseline (your current generator), Redwood hosted baseline (small run to validate config), and Dedicated pilot runs with different batching/quant profiles. We'll capture p50,p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens. Also measure cold-start behaviour and cache warm-up.
[06:35] Sofia: Sounds good. Timeline? We want a 4-week pilot.
[06:40] Maya: Proposed timeline: week 0 (this week) - share traces and requirements; week 1 - Redwood sizing + pilot config and pricing; week 2 - deploy Dedicated pilot and run initial benchmarks; weeks 3-4 - full pilot with A/B and monitoring; final review end of week 4.
[06:58] Priya: If we can start provisioning quickly, that works. Darius, any procurement hurdles?
[07:03] Darius: We'll need SOW and SLA details; security checklist is standard — SOC 2, data handling, SAML for SSO.
[07:12] Maya: We'll attach security docs and a standard SOW template with Dedicated details.

[07:20] Liam: Back to unit economics — we'll produce a per-token estimate showing a range: worst-case (no batching, no cache), typical-case (expected batch sizes and cache hits), and best-case (high batching, high cache). Example numbers are illustrative: worst-case $0.035/1k tokens, typical $0.012/1k tokens, best-case $0.006/1k tokens, depending heavily on model and batch.
[07:49] Sofia: Those ranges help. Can you break out where most savings come from?
[07:52] Liam: Biggest wins are: batching (for short tokens), KV/prefix caching, and using quantized models. Also routing policy — e.g., serve lower-criticality flows on cheaper model variants.
[08:05] Priya: Can Redwood do automatic fallback if capacity constrained? We don't want timeouts during peaks.
[08:10] Maya: Yes, we support fallback policies: route to a smaller model or queued degraded mode, and we can set graceful degradation thresholds. We'll include recommendations in the pilot SLOs.

[08:22] Darius: On instrumentation: we need tracing hooks and OpenTelemetry-compatible logs.
[08:27] Liam: Redwood Console exposes tracing hooks and you can attach OpenTelemetry spans — we'll provide an example integration.

[08:36] Priya: For the A/B, do you recommend making real customers part of it or a shadow test?
[08:40] Maya: Start with shadow/holding out a small percent — do internal QA and ramp to live gradually. We'll help design the ramp.

[08:50] Sofia: One more operational Q — do you support per-tenant limits so one promo spike doesn't blow budget?
[08:55] Liam: Yes, per-route quotas and rate limits are configurable, plus automated burst controls on Dedicated.

[09:03] Priya: Great. Let's talk specifics we'll need in the trace file. Darius?
[09:07] Darius: We will include: per-request timestamp, token counts, user-agent, prompt template id, and a label for intent. We'll sanitize user IDs.

[09:18] Maya: Perfect. After we get the trace we'll run a synthetic replay to estimate batching distribution and cache hit rates. We'll share a sizing calc and expected per-token numbers.

[09:30] (brief cross-talk about calendar invites)

[09:45] Priya: If the pilot shows 10%+ conversion uplift with cost under $25k, we greenlight Dedicated for Q4.
[09:54] Maya: That's a clear success criterion — we'll include conversion delta, p95 below 300ms, and total pilot cost under $25k as acceptance metrics.

[10:05] Liam: We'll also track inference error rates and model regressions via per-prompt eval hooks.

[10:12] Darius: Anything else on procurement? We need a SAML integration timeline.
[10:16] Maya: SAML docs will be shared; provisioning for Dedicated typically 3-5 business days after agreement.

[10:24] Sofia: Ok. On the model side, do you recommend single model type or mix?
[10:27] Liam: Mix. Use a higher-quality model for checkout flows and a smaller quantized model for low-risk microcopy. We'll show routing rules in sizing.

[10:38] Priya: Can Redwood give a sample A/B dashboard?
[10:40] Maya: Yes — we'll attach a sample Redwood Console dashboard template for pilot metrics (latency curves, token cost, per-route spend, quality evals).

[10:50] (silence while someone scribbles notes)

[11:00] Maya: Quick recap of action items: Darius will share traces; Maya sends pricing and SOW; Liam runs initial bench once he has traces; Priya confirms metrics and stakeholders. Anything to add?
[11:14] Sofia: That's it from our side. Thanks.
[11:18] Maya: Great, we'll follow up inside 48 hours with the spreadsheet and SOW.

[11:25] (meeting wrap; informal goodbyes)

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcription had a few mis-heard words around model names and GPU types; speakers occasionally overlapped.

Bench plan appendix (auto-generated):
- Input: 7-day trace replay sanitized; sample size 10k user prompts across templates; 3 model variants (7B quant, 13B float, 7B float)
- Metrics captured: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, cache-hit %, batch sizes distribution, error rates.
- Run order: baseline -> hosted small-run -> dedicated runs (varied batch/quant settings) -> A/B ramp.
